justifications.functional_suitability: Scheduling Container with Reservation Service (atomic locks), EMR Container, Billing Container and Immutable Audit Storage Sink cover R-02 to R-04. But no patient registration/admission component exists for R-01, the EMR audit trail is indirect, and Patient Portal is thin.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Event Broker gives asynchronous decoupling, PgBouncer Connection Pooler and Gateway Cache Client (Redis) help efficiency. But there is no EMR read cache, no autoscaling or replicas, no explicit <1s P95 mechanism, and synchronous audit writes and WAF redaction add latency.
justifications.compatibility: FHIR Interoperability Adapter in EMR Container handles HL7 FHIR with External Labs/Imaging Vendors over TLS; Billing Container uses secure REST to Insurance Clearinghouses. Schema Registry Validator helps event contracts. Minor gaps: no FHIR server or API versioning details.
justifications.usability: All five personas have web/mobile access via WAF Container and Patient Portal Container, and Notification Container supports multi-channel alerts. But there are no dedicated staff UIs, no role-specific interfaces, no accessibility mechanisms, and the Patient Portal is the only frontend.
justifications.reliability: Patroni/etcd gives database failover and Event Broker decouples services. However the database is active-passive, contradicting the active-active 99.99% requirement. No multi-region deployment, replicas, backup/DR, circuit breakers, or HA for the WAF, Gateway and Vault is shown.
justifications.security: MFA with OIDC via Auth Validator, WAF Engine, mTLS via SPIFFE/SPIRE, Vault Transit (AES-256) and Database Secrets Engine, field-level PHI encryption, pgaudit, WORM Storage Controller with 10-year retention, Data Masking Engine and row-level security match HIPAA/GDPR needs.
justifications.maintainability: Clear microservice decomposition (EMR, Scheduling, Billing, Notification, Analytics) with event-driven low coupling and an Event Broker with Schema Registry Validator. Minor issues: shared PostgreSQL Databases across services, Billing component duplicates its container, and Kafka/RabbitMQ is left undecided.
justifications.portability: Kubernetes-based containers, Vault, MinIO/S3 Object Lock, and cert-manager suit on-prem-k8s and eu-central-1. But there are no explicit deployment views, no hybrid replication or failover across environments, and some choices stay undecided (Kafka/RabbitMQ, S3/MinIO).

sensitivity_points: No EMR data cache; every screen hits PostgreSQL
Field-level encryption via Vault adds latency per read
tradeoffs: Field-level PHI encryption and WAF redaction versus latency
Single active database node limits read scaling

sensitivity_points: FHIR ingestion is synchronous in EMR, competing with screen loads
Single active database writer under bulk load
tradeoffs: Broker decoupling helps but ingestion is not isolated from EMR reads
PERF-02.justification: FHIR adapter and broker exist, but ingestion runs inside the EMR container with no separate ingest path, no read replicas and no throttling. Isolation from screen load is unaddressed.

sensitivity_points: Active-passive database; no cross-site replication or global traffic routing described
tradeoffs: Active-passive simplicity versus zero data loss and active-active requirement
AVAIL-01.justification: No multi-site deployment, global load balancer or cross-site synchronous replication is modelled. Patroni is active-passive and the brief demands active-active. Zero data loss and 1 minute restoration are not supported.

sensitivity_points: Patroni failover time versus 30 s target
No idempotency or claim retry mechanism modelled
tradeoffs: Asynchronous replication risks data loss versus synchronous latency
AVAIL-02.justification: Patroni provides automated failover, and the broker can support retries. However, no idempotency keys, outbox or transactional claim handling is shown, so duplicates or losses are possible. Failover under 30 s is unverified.

sensitivity_points: Billing component is monolithic; clearinghouse integration is not separated
tradeoffs: Billing microservice isolates EMR but couples integrations inside billing
MOD-01.justification: EMR is isolated from Billing, so EMR stays unchanged. But Billing is one undifferentiated component with no clearinghouse adapter abstraction, so the change is confined to the container, not one integration component.

sensitivity_points: Event schemas in registry need updating too
tradeoffs: Shared database eases change but couples services
MOD-02.justification: Change touches the EMR data manager, database schema, frontend and event schema, which is plausible within three or four components. pgaudit captures DML automatically, helping the audit trail. No registration or demographics component exists, though, and migration tooling is absent.

sensitivity_points: MFA enforcement point and identity provider not explicit
No alerting component for failed attempts within 1 minute
tradeoffs: Strong perimeter checks add request latency
SEC-01.justification: Flows specify OAuth2/OIDC with MFA and token validation at the gateway, denying access without the second factor. Failed attempts are logged, but no identity provider or security alerting mechanism is modelled, so the 1-minute alert is unaddressed.

sensitivity_points: Row-level security gives no treating-relationship policy check
EMR container has no explicit link to audit sink
pgaudit logs do not reach the sink
tradeoffs: Auditing every read adds latency and storage volume
SEC-02.justification: WORM storage with 10-year retention and pgaudit exist, plus row-level security. But the EMR-to-audit-sink path is not modelled, and pgaudit is not connected to the sink. A treating-relationship policy check is not explicit, so 100% read audit is not assured.
